ux.lcopyb.runtimeError.blockedTitle: Your AI service blocked this request
ux.lcopyb.runtimeError.blockedBody: Your AI service's content checks stopped this request. Review your request before sending a new message. Changing the bot's level will not lift that check.
ux.lcopyb.runtimeError.recovery: Review the details, then retry or pick another model in {page}.
ux.lcopyb.errorPreview.blocked: Your AI service blocked this request.
ux.lcopyb.engines.chooseCopy: Choose a copy found on this computer…
ux.lcopyb.engines.availabilityNote: Turning an engine on or off restarts it and stops its replies in progress. Sometimes other engines restart too. Turning one on may run it once to check it works. Work that stopped earlier does not start again by itself.
ux.lcopyb.engines.commandLinesSubtitle: Use Choose location to point an engine at a specific copy of its app, such as a particular version or another program that starts it. Give its full location. Saving restarts that engine and stops its replies in progress. Sometimes other engines restart too.
ux.lcopyb.engines.noneFound: No AI apps found on this computer yet.
ux.lcopyb.engines.sameApp: Uses the same app; this account is kept separately.
ux.lcopyb.level.unlimitedHere: In conversations you start, runs commands and tools without asking, including reading and sending your keys. It still asks before a wipe it can read and before a command it cannot read in full. A script file can still run unread. That includes this computer. Publishing, browser payments and new email recipients keep their own approvals. Everyone else's messages, other bots, trigger links from other apps and your channel messages keep the cards they have now. A routine runs at this level or its own, whichever is lower, and keeps its cards.
ux.lcopyb.level.unlimited: In conversations you start, runs commands and tools without asking, including reading and sending your keys. It still asks before a wipe it can read and before a command it cannot read in full. A script file can still run unread. Publishing, browser payments and new email recipients keep their own approvals. Everyone else's messages, other bots, trigger links from other apps and your channel messages keep the cards they have now. A routine runs at this level or its own, whichever is lower, and keeps its cards.
ux.lcopyb.level.fullHere: Keeps going without asking, including on this computer and before contacting other bots. Still asks before paying, emailing someone new, posting in public, deleting outside its folder, or reading your keys and passwords. Work started by another app's trigger link still asks. Routines keep their own level and never run above this one.
ux.lcopyb.level.full: Keeps going without asking, including before contacting other bots. Still asks before paying, emailing someone new, posting in public, deleting outside its folder, or reading your keys and passwords. Work started by another app's trigger link still asks. Routines keep their own level and never run above this one.
ux.lcopyb.level.channelHint: On unless you turn it off. Group chats, other people and trigger links from other apps still ask. Routines use their own level.
ux.lcopyb.level.peerSkip: On, but {level} skips this in conversations you start and in routines at that level; work started by another app's trigger link still stops and asks. Switch to Auto to be asked every time.
ux.lcopyb.fullAccess.stillAsks: Work started by another app's trigger link still asks, as it does in Auto.
ux.lcopyb.houseRules.untrusted: A message from a channel, another app's trigger link or a web page can't approve anything or give a bot more access. Full access approves on its own, so give it only to bots you trust with that.
ux.lcopyb.cloud.claudeSignin: Cloud chats use a long-lasting Claude sign-in. Your local connected tools work as before; claude.ai connectors and Remote Control are desktop features and are not part of Cloud chats.
ux.lcopyb.connected.subtitleDesktop: One Flux Router key connects {apps}. You can add your own connected tools too.
ux.lcopyb.connected.subtitleRemote: View your connected apps. Manage them and your connected tools in the desktop app.
